RGV Multi-Tech Services • Architecture & Executive Overview Page 2 of 17

1. Executive Summary & System Architecture

RGV-System is an enterprise-grade, multi-platform business operations management system engineered specifically for RGV Multi-Tech Services. The system unifies four core business operations—Customer Service Bookings, Physical Inventory & Asset Management, Field Equipment Borrowing & Returns, and Business Analytics & Compliance—into a synchronized ecosystem powered by a single source of truth database.

The Core Operational Vision: Customers submit and track technical service requests publicly without account friction; field employees manage assigned dispatches, review inventory, scan physical equipment via native Android QR scanning, and process returns on-site; administrators retain end-to-end command over approvals, stock thresholds, role-based security, automated backups, AI-driven demand forecasts, and tamper-evident audit trails.

1.1 Multi-Surface Ecosystem Architecture

Unlike disjointed solutions that rely on batch synchronization workers or independent data stores, the RGV System connects all client surfaces directly to a unified PostgreSQL engine (hosted on Supabase) sharing identical business constraints, relations, and transactional integrity.

Unified Multi-Surface Architecture
Public Web Portal No-auth Bookings & Tracking
↔
Laravel 12 MVC Core PHP 8.2+, Breeze, Spatie RBAC
↔
Supabase PostgreSQL 33+ Tables, Triggers, RPCs
Employee Web Portal Assigned Bookings & Requests
↔
Flutter Android App Direct RPCs + QR Scanner
↔
Admin Command Center Analytics, Backups, AI Tools

1.2 Core Architectural Principles

  • Zero-Sync Discrepancy: Both web and mobile surfaces query and mutate the exact same live tables, eliminating data divergence.
  • Defense-in-Depth Security: Layered protection spanning global HTTPS enforcement, security headers, CSRF tokens, strict Eloquent ORM parameterized queries, and granular Spatie permissions.
  • Hermetic Test Isolation: The PHPUnit test harness is completely decoupled from production credentials, executing strictly in-memory via SQLite.

2. Role-Based Access & Public Customer Portal

The system implements a strictly segregated role hierarchy. Public users interact without authentication to eliminate customer friction, while internal staff and administrators are protected by Spatie Role-Based Access Control (RBAC), multi-factor authentication (MFA), and session monitors.

2.1 Stakeholder Matrix & Operational Privileges

Role Client Platform Accessible Features Security Controls
Public Web Browser (Desktop & Mobile) Submit service booking requests, track booking progress in real-time, scan public inventory QR verification tokens, browse services. Zero credentials required; public rate throttling (30 req/min); CSRF protection; input sanitization.
Employee Web Portal + Flutter Android App Manage assigned service jobs, create equipment borrow requisitions, conduct stock checks, process returns, view notifications. Password hashing (Bcrypt); Mandatory MFA (TOTP / Email); Sanctum bearer token; Supabase AAL2 JWT; session timeout.
Administrator Admin Web Control Center Full oversight: approve/reject bookings, assign staff, manage inventory, execute backups, audit logs, AI forecasting, site settings. Admin middleware; MFA protection; Force-logout capability; Impersonation audit tracking; Password-confirmed deletion.

2.2 Public Booking Submission Engine

Customers can request service visits through an intuitive, mobile-responsive booking form accessible directly from the homepage (/booking). The interface is tailored to capture complete technical and scheduling specifications upfront.

Customer Information Captured
  • Full Customer Name: Contact person for service delivery.
  • Valid Email Address: Destination for instant lifecycle email alerts.
  • Contact Telephone: Direct phone number for technician field coordination.
  • Physical Service Address: Precise destination for on-site execution.
Service & Scheduling Parameters
  • Preferred Execution Date: Requested service calendar date.
  • Preferred Time Window: Morning / afternoon time slot selection.
  • Purpose Category: Installation, Maintenance, Repair, or Inspection.
  • Reason & Technical Notes: Detailed problem or work description.
Automated Reference Token Generation: Upon successful submission, the system issues a unique, tamper-resistant reference identifier formatted as BK-XXXXXXXXXXXXX (e.g., BK-20261025-A8F9). This reference code serves as the customer's permanent lookup key.

RGV Multi-Tech Services • Tracking & QR Asset Verification Page 5 of 17

2.3 Public Real-Time Service Tracking & Verification

Customers can monitor their service request at any time by visiting /booking/track/{reference} or entering their reference code on the homepage tracking form. The tracker reveals live operational milestones:

1. Pending ReviewAwaiting Admin

Request logged in database. Awaiting administrative review for technician availability, parts, and schedule feasibility.

2. Approved & AssignedTechnician Set

Admin confirmed schedule. Designated technician is assigned, notified, and preparing required technical tools.

3. CompletedService Finalized

Technician executed work on-site, filed field remarks, and marked booking successfully fulfilled.

2.4 Alternative Lifecycle Outcomes

• Rejected Bookings

If a service request cannot be fulfilled (e.g. out of service territory, fully booked date), administrators document a mandatory reason. The customer tracking screen transparently presents this explanation along with support contact numbers.

• Cancelled Requests

Bookings cancelled prior to execution are clearly tagged with cancellation timestamps and logged in the system audit trail, automatically freeing up technician scheduling slots.

2.5 Public QR Code Asset Verification

Physical equipment and tools managed by RGV Multi-Tech Services feature permanent, weather-resistant QR code labels linking to immutable public tokens (/inventory/qr/{token}). When scanned by clients or site inspectors:

  • Authentication of Authenticity: Confirms the equipment is officially owned, calibrated, and maintained by RGV Multi-Tech Services.
  • Non-Sensitive Specifications Displayed: Reveals asset model, equipment category, unit specifications, and service compatibility.
  • Security Redaction: Sensitive internal warehouse details—including purchase prices, internal supplier references, and available stock quantities—are strictly hidden from public lookup.
No-Login Frictionless Customer Experience: The public portal requires no user registration, password creation, or email verification to book services. All access is keyed to the customer's secure booking reference code.

RGV Multi-Tech Services • Employee Web Portal Operations Page 6 of 17

3. Employee Operations: Web Portal Workspace

Employees represent the core field service workforce. They utilize a dedicated Web Portal (/employee) for dispatch review, customer details, and equipment requisitions, paired with a companion Flutter Android App for mobility on the job site.

3.1 Employee Web Portal Modules

• Technician Command Dashboard

Centralized home screen displaying active assigned service bookings, pending equipment requisitions, items currently borrowed, overdue return alerts, and an unread notification counter.

• Assigned Dispatch Management

Technicians view complete customer details, service locations, and scheduling requirements. They can append job remarks, document field progress, and mark bookings as Completed upon job fulfillment.

• Equipment Requisition (Borrow System)

Searchable inventory catalog with real-time stock availability. Technicians submit multi-item borrow requests specifying required quantities, operational purpose, borrow start date, and expected return due date.

• Return & Condition Reporting

Itemized return workflow allowing staff to declare returned item condition (Good, Fair, Poor), document damage notes, specify warehouse return locations, and soft-delete closed records.

3.2 Equipment Requisition Workflow Rules

The borrow request system enforces strict business logic to prevent equipment loss, tool hoarding, or double-allocation:

Requisition Stage System Validation & Behavior Operational Impact
Catalog Browsing Displays real-time available stock (total quantity minus currently reserved and borrowed units). Prevents requesting items that are out of stock or reserved for other jobs.
Draft Submission Staff specifies item quantities, borrow start date, expected return date, and job reason. Request created in pending status; items immediately reserved.
Admin Decision Admin reviews requisition. Approval sets status to approved; rejection releases reservation. Staff notified via email and in-app alert immediately upon decision.
Overdue Monitoring System evaluates expected return date against current timestamp. Past-due requests automatically flagged as overdue with alerts sent to staff.
Self-Service Cleanliness: Employees can soft-delete their own returned or rejected borrow requests from their personal list, maintaining a clutter-free view while preserving full administrative audit trails.

3.3 Flutter Android Mobile Application (Field Operations)

The native Android app in mobile/ is purpose-built for technicians working in equipment yards, service vans, and customer facilities. Built with Flutter, it operates independently of the web application server by interacting directly with Supabase PostgreSQL.

Mobile Feature Implementation Mechanism Field Technician Benefit
Hardware QR Scanner Integrated mobile_scanner with hardware camera acceleration. Point-and-shoot barcode/QR recognition on physical tool labels; zero typing required.
Manual Item Lookup Alphanumeric code search with real-time substring filtering. Instant fallback for scratched, dirty, or damaged QR tags, or low-light field conditions.
Direct Supabase RPCs Transactional stored procedures: borrow_request, return_items. App continues functioning even if the Laravel web application is restarting or offline.
Stock Reservation Automated atomic decrement of available quantity upon request. Prevents multiple technicians from reserving the same critical tools simultaneously.
Idempotent Returns Client-side UUID generation via Dart uuid package. Guarantees that poor network connectivity or double-tapping never creates duplicate return logs.
Mobile Security & MFA Supabase Auth with mandatory TOTP MFA (AAL2 compliance). High security; credentials encrypted using flutter_secure_storage.

3.4 Equipment Lifecycle Workflow

Equipment Lifecycle Workflow
1. Item Requisition Technician scans QR or selects items
→
2. Stock Reservation Items held in pending status
→
3. Admin Approval Stock officially released as Borrowed
4. Field Execution Tools utilized during service
→
5. Return & Condition Good/Fair/Poor rating + Damage log
→
6. Stock Restoration Items returned to active inventory
Dual Mobile API Architecture: In addition to native Supabase RPCs, the Laravel backend maintains authenticated REST endpoints under /api/v1/mobile/* (protected by Laravel Sanctum bearer tokens with dedicated rate limiting of 20 req/min for auth and 120 req/min for operational endpoints) to support external integrations and legacy clients.

4.3 Inventory Management & Equipment Governance

The inventory management module tracks all physical tools, technical instruments, machinery, replacement parts, and consumable supplies across warehouse storage locations.

Comprehensive Asset Tracking
  • Catalog Attributes: Item Code, Name, Category, Quantity, Unit (pcs, box, kg), Unit Cost, Location, and Status.
  • Physical Condition: Categorized as New, Good, Fair, or Poor.
  • Permanent QR Code Generator: Generates unique vector QR tags for asset labeling (simplesoftwareio/simple-qrcode).
Thresholds & Low-Stock Prevention
  • Configurable Thresholds: Set minimum stock warnings per item.
  • Dedicated Low-Stock Screen: Filter and review all items requiring urgent reordering (/admin/inventories/low-stock).
  • Automated Administrator Alerts: Trigger notifications when stock drops below minimum operating limits.

4.4 Equipment Borrow Request Governance

Administrators maintain complete custody oversight of all equipment deployed into the field:

Governance Action Administrative Inspection & Criteria System Execution
Approval / Rejection Inspect requesting technician, purpose, project site, and requested duration. Approval deducts active stock; rejection releases reserved units immediately.
Overdue Tracking Review borrow requests whose due date has elapsed without item check-in. Triggers overdue status flags and sends reminder notifications to technicians.
Condition Auditing Compare return condition against check-out condition (e.g. Good → Damaged). Logs wear-and-tear records and initiates maintenance tickets if damaged.
Drop-off Verification Confirm physical equipment returned to designated warehouse shelf or bin. Restores quantity to available inventory catalog.
Asset Protection: No tool can be checked out without an approved borrow request. Every equipment transaction records the technician ID, timestamp, expected return date, and condition report.

5.1 User Administration & Identity Management

Feature Operational Mechanism Administrative Utility

5.2 Multi-Entity Trash & Soft-Delete Management

To prevent accidental permanent data loss, the system incorporates a centralized trash management engine (/admin/trash) covering 5 key entity types:

Entity Type Soft-Delete Protection Administrative Recovery Actions
Bookings Cancelled or deleted customer service bookings. One-click restoration to active listings or password-confirmed permanent purge.
Borrow Requests Completed or rejected equipment requisitions. Restore historical borrow requests or securely delete after audit retention.
Inventory Items Decommissioned tools or depleted parts. Restore items with full stock histories intact, or permanently delete.
Inventory Categories Removed equipment categories. Restores category relationships without corrupting associated item records.
User Accounts Removed employee or administrator profiles. Restores credentials and historical assignments safely.
Password-Verified Deletion: Permanent deletion of any item from the trash requires re-entry of administrative credentials, preventing rogue or accidental data destruction.

5.3 Automated Disaster Recovery, Backups & Auditing

RGV-System incorporates automated disaster recovery routines powered by spatie/laravel-backup and an immutable, cryptographic audit trail.

Automated Scheduled Backups

Scheduled Automation

• Daily Full Backup: Database + Application files at 2:00 AM.
• Weekly DB Snapshot: Sundays at 3:00 AM.
• Automated Cleanup: Daily at 3:30 AM enforcing retention rules.

SHA-256 Integrity

Every backup ZIP file is hashed with SHA-256. Administrators can trigger a one-click cryptographic verification to guarantee archives are corruption-free and uncompromised.

Cloud Storage & Alerts

• Direct ZIP download from admin panel.
• Optional Amazon S3 cloud replication.
• Automated email alerts to administrator upon backup completion or failure.

Strict Retention Policy: Retains all backups for 1 day, daily backups for 7 days, weekly snapshots for 4 weeks, monthly archives for 12 months, and yearly milestones for 2 years, enforcing an automatic 5,000 MB storage cap.

5.4 Tamper-Evident Cryptographic Audit Trail

The system logs all administrative, technician, and model operations in a secure audit log (/admin/audit-logs):

Audit Component Mechanism & Implementation Compliance & Security Value
HMAC-SHA256 Chaining Each log entry computes a cryptographic hash over timestamp, user ID, event, and prior hash. Prevents database tampering: modifying any historical record breaks the cryptographic chain.
Model Mutation Tracking Spatie ActivityLog records old and new values on all Eloquent model updates. Provides complete accountability of who changed stock counts, prices, or statuses.
Security Events Logs login successes, failed password attempts, MFA events, and impersonation starts/stops. Enables instant forensic investigation during suspicious access incidents.
Compliance Export One-click CSV and PDF export of audit entries with date range filters. Simplifies external operational audits and regulatory compliance.

6. Analytics, Bulk Data Operations & AI Intelligence

RGV-System equips managers with actionable business intelligence through multi-domain reporting, asynchronous bulk data ingestion/export, and a robust, multi-tier Artificial Intelligence engine.

6.1 Business Reporting & Analytics Engine

Report Domain Metrics Analyzed & Visualized Supported Export Formats
Bookings Report Total service volume, completion rates, cancellation ratios, popular purpose categories, and technician performance. PDF (formatted table), Excel (.xlsx), CSV, JSON.
Inventory Report Total catalog valuation, stock levels by category, low-stock threshold status, and item condition distributions. PDF (formatted table), Excel (.xlsx), CSV, JSON.
Borrow Requests Report Requisition trends, most borrowed tools, overdue frequency, employee utilization, and return condition ratios. PDF (formatted table), Excel (.xlsx), CSV, JSON.

6.2 High-Capacity Bulk Import & Export Engine

Bulk Ingestion Engine (Imports)

Mass-import inventory catalogs and user directories from CSV or Excel spreadsheets (/admin/import-export). Features downloadable standard templates and intelligent duplicate-handling:

  • Skip: Ignores duplicate items while importing new entries.
  • Update: Refreshes existing records with updated stock/prices.
  • Abort: Stops execution on syntax or validation errors.
  • Error Logs: Download row-by-row failure reports with error notes.
Custom Data Export Builder

Export complete databases or filtered slices with custom column selection:

  • Asynchronous Background Queuing: Large exports process via Laravel Queues without freezing HTTP requests.
  • Multi-Format: Formatted PDF tables, Microsoft Excel (.xlsx), and raw CSV.
  • Export Audit Logs: Tracks who requested exports and when files were downloaded.
Queued Export Execution: High-volume exports containing thousands of records execute in background worker queues (ExportLog model), allowing managers to continue working without browser timeouts.

6.3 Multi-Tier Artificial Intelligence (AI) Suite

The system incorporates a multi-provider fallback architecture ensuring AI tools remain available regardless of external API outages or rate limits:

Multi-Tier AI Provider Fallback Architecture
Tier 1: Ollama Local Private, Zero Latency (llama3.1)
→
Tier 2: Google Gemini gemini-2.0-flash (Cloud Intelligence)
→
Tier 3: OpenAI GPT openai-php Secondary Fallback
→
Tier 4: Rule-Based Deterministic System Fallback

Core AI Capabilities

1. Operational Chatbot

Admin chatbot answering contextual operational questions (e.g., "Which equipment is currently overdue?", "How many repair bookings are scheduled for this week?") grounded in live database queries.

2. Predictive Booking Forecast

Predictive analysis of historical booking patterns, seasonal spikes, and customer demand curves, providing staffing and dispatch recommendations for coming months.

3. Inventory Optimization

AI algorithms calculate optimal reorder points, flag fast-depleting consumables before stock-outs occur, and highlight stagnant tools to maximize capital efficiency.

AI Architecture Highlights

Component Technical Implementation Operational Advantage
Context Grounding Queries execute parameterized aggregate queries on PostgreSQL prior to LLM synthesis. Eliminates hallucination; all answers reflect factual, real-time database numbers.
Data Privacy Primary provider is a local Ollama instance running inside the private infrastructure. Proprietary client details and booking records never leave the local network.
Access Restriction Chatbot API (/api/chatbot/query) is rate-limited (30 req/min) and locked to Admin sessions. Prevents unauthorized probing or token depletion by unauthenticated callers.
Continuous Availability: If local Ollama is offline, requests cascade automatically to Google Gemini 2.0 Flash, then OpenAI, and finally internal rule-based algorithms, ensuring zero downtime.

7. Omnichannel Notifications & System Configuration

The system ensures tight coordination across customers, field technicians, and management through a dual-channel notification architecture and a centralized 7-tab system configuration suite.

7.1 Complete 14-Class Notification Directory

Every significant business event triggers a dedicated notification class dispatching alerts across both in-app notification bells and responsive HTML transactional emails:

Notification Class Target Recipient Triggering Event Operational Action Conveyed
NewBookingReceived Admin Customer submits public booking. Alerts dispatchers to review schedule and assign technician.
BookingApproved Customer Admin approves service booking. Confirms service date, time slot, and booking reference.
BookingRejected Customer Admin declines service booking. Explains specific reason for refusal and alternative options.
BookingAssigned Employee Admin allocates technician to job. Transmits client contact info, service address, and scope of work.
BookingCompleted Customer & Admin Technician marks job finished. Sends final service summary and generates billing invoice.
BookingCancelled Admin & Employee Booking cancelled by party. Releases technician schedule and cancels preparation.
NewBorrowRequestReceived Admin Technician requests tools. Alerts warehouse manager to review and authorize tool release.
BorrowRequestApproved Employee Admin approves equipment release. Instructs technician that tools are ready for pickup.
BorrowRequestRejected Employee Admin rejects equipment release. Provides reason (e.g., equipment reserved for higher priority).
BorrowRequestBorrowed Employee Items handed over to technician. Logs custody transfer and sets active due date clock.
BorrowRequestReturned Admin & Employee Equipment returned to storage. Confirms stock restoration and records condition ratings.
LowStockAlert Admin Item quantity ≤ threshold. Warns managers to replenish critical tools or consumables.
UserStatusChanged Employee Admin activates/deactivates user. Notifies user of account privilege updates.
Per-User Preference Matrix: Users can customize their alert experience in their profile (NotificationPreference model). Each user independently toggles Email Delivery and In-App Delivery for every notification type according to their personal workflow.

Settings Tab Configurable Parameters System Impact
